episode.subject: Oncorhynchus nerka
episode.title: When I saw him again
episode.body:
We had come through the shallow place together. When I saw his red back again, I went towards it.

Then I saw her.

He turned across me. I opened my mouth. He opened his.

I had remembered the two of us pushing forward. He was close enough to touch now, and neither of us would let the other pass.

I bit.

For a moment I was holding on to someone I had been glad to see.

proposals.visibleScene: Two red spawning sockeye contend near surface, with a green hooked head and open mouth pressed against the other fish at left. Water churns around their bodies and fins. Eye, jaw, red back and physical contact legible; splashes obscure parts of bodies. No female can be securely singled out.
proposals.fictionBoundary: Recognition, shared earlier passage, attraction to off-frame female, approach order, reciprocal challenge and conflicted memory are invented. FWS identifies males fighting for mates. Do not claim documented individual recognition, a photographed female or a measured bite outcome. The narrator is the clearly visible hooked-head fish.
proposals.continuity: Append after sole admitted What I remembered, during spawning-ground competition but before any personal completed spawning or death. The previously anonymous companion is fictionally recognized here; earlier wording stays intact. Preserve male sockeye identity, Lake Clark watershed home and adult avatar. Izembek source provenance is separate; no trip from Lake Clark to Izembek is asserted.
proposals.authorReview: The image supplies the actual bodily clash; the episode changes a companion into a rival without reducing either fish to a joke. The earlier moment of shared effort now complicates the bite. Biological aggression is not suppressed to preserve a sentimental friendship. No suffering punchline, moral or invented anatomical faculty.
proposals.biologyEvidence: Primary NPS ranger account independently read: males fight for female access during spawning; sockeye spawn and subsequently die. This episode does not add post-spawning survival.

heldDrafts.body: I climbed down because she would not stop moving. The rock stayed perfectly still. I stood on it a while, enjoying how right I had been. An arm passed above me. I lifted a claw towards it, then remembered why I was down here. She moved it away. I followed.
heldDrafts.reason: Moving-host annoyance followed by wanting contact again overlaps A little less still. Kept as a rejected attempt, not canon.
